description: Restructure batch-2 n=4096 graph replay into two independent per-matrix DAG chains so one matrix's narrow MathDx factor and quarter-panel solve nodes overlap the other's full-SM CuTe rank-k waves. Use direct graph dependencies and staggered releases rather than batch-wide synchronization while preserving the n=256 leader, cp.async large shapes, every other dispatch, caller-stream semantics, caches, fresh inputs, and the full grid.

Split batch-2 n4096 factor, quarter-panel solve, and CuTe rank-k work into two sample-local streams with alternating event dependencies; slice build passed, but the local banned-stream gate rejected newly introduced literal stream spellings before Modal validation.

Policy-clean two-chain n4096 DAG: sample-local one-CTA factor and 64-CTA quarter-panel solve launches, one-matrix CuTe rank-k waves, and alternating event releases so narrow work for one matrix can overlap the other matrix's ordered full-SM update. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 benchmark cells passed. Batch2/n4096 measured 1889.890 us; aggregate measured 777.605 us versus parent aggregate 768.640 us.

Removed cross-chain rank-k serialization from Trial1 while retaining the post-first-narrow release edge and graph fork/join. Both sample-local chains then advanced independently, allowing a next narrow stage to become ready while the other sample still occupied the wide path. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 improved from 1889.890 to 1874.712 us; aggregate measured 777.987 us versus Trial1 777.605 and parent 768.640.

Split each independent sample chain across a high-priority narrow queue and default-priority CuTe queue, with one ready/done event pair per 256-wide stage and the same post-first-narrow second-chain release. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 improved from Trial2 1874.712 to 1843.072 us; aggregate improved from 777.987 to 774.769 us versus parent 768.640.

Moved the second sample's one-time release edge from the end of sample0's first 256-wide narrow stage to immediately after its first profiled grid1 factor, reducing the initial stagger from roughly 184 profiled us to 20.48 us while retaining high-priority narrow/default-priority wide queues and independent chains thereafter. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 improved from Trial3 1843.072 to 1767.933 us; aggregate improved from 774.769 to 772.990 us versus parent 768.640. The sole hosted index11 request on exact Trial1 4c1ae8c succeeded as job ad0549e7cd82402a8cb70f27a87fe102: factor stages were 20.48/23.17/25.47/27.97 us at grid1, 56 registers, 55.30 KiB shared, and solves were 16.51/19.74/23.39/26.94 us at grid64, 120 registers, 55.30 KiB shared, around 12.5% occupancy and 71-72% no-eligible. Canonical artifacts end in 4c1ae8c62dc52033d248cc61208977dca5317d64 under the run profile directory.

Removed the remaining one-time post-first-factor release edge so both high-priority narrow chains start together, retaining per-stage narrow-to-wide handoffs and independent sample dependencies. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 regressed from Trial4 1767.933 to 1790.960 us, confirming the profiled 20-us first-factor stagger improves scheduling; aggregate was outlier-inflated to 787.386 us with untouched n256/n512/n1024/n2048 cells also slower.

Completed the initial-stagger bracket by releasing sample1 after sample0's first grid1 factor plus first grid64 solve, roughly 37 profiled us, while retaining the Trial3 high/default-priority split. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 measured 1793.465 us, above post-factor Trial4's 1767.933 and near equal-start Trial5's 1790.960; aggregate measured 776.620 us amid an untouched n256 outlier. The post-factor edge remains the measured target winner.

Restored the measured post-factor release and right-sized each sample-local solve grid from fixed 64 blocks to the exact remaining tile count. Slice build, policy gate, all 17 tests, and fresh-input guard passed, but the full benchmark failed at batch2/n4096 before GPU launch because Numba's launcher rejected the capture-time np.int32 grid value 63 instead of a native integer; no aggregate metric was emitted.

Converted Trial7's exact live solve-grid counts to native integers and measured the intended post-factor-staggered topology: grids shrink from 63 through 1 blocks instead of launching a fixed 64 with inactive workers. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 measured 1790.490 us, above fixed-grid Trial4's 1767.933 us; aggregate measured 773.379 us. The inactive fixed-grid tails therefore schedule better than 63 distinct underfilled launch configurations.

Restored fixed 64-block solve grids and kept the post-first-factor four-queue DAG, but changed the two narrow queues from high to default priority to isolate the priority contribution. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 measured 1771.198 us, only 3.265 us above high-priority Trial4's 1767.933 and within target noise; aggregate measured 771.928 us versus Trial4 772.990 under favorable untouched-cell sampling. Queue separation and the post-factor edge account for nearly all measured gain, with priority a small target-floor effect.

Applied the profile-selected post-factor release edge at every 256-wide stage with high-priority narrow queues, keeping sample0 roughly one factor ahead of sample1 throughout the captured DAG. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 measured 1771.522 us, 3.589 us above Trial4's one-time-release 1767.933 and noise-flat with equal-priority Trial9's 1771.198; aggregate measured 772.464 us. Repeated cross-chain releases add no target-floor gain over the single initial stagger.

Alternated the leading sample at each 256-wide stage: sample0 released sample1 after its first factor on even stages, and sample1 released sample0 on odd stages, with high-priority narrow queues and independent wide nodes. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 regressed sharply to 1902.458 us from sample0-leading Trial10 1771.522 and one-time Trial4 1767.933; aggregate measured 778.153 us. Alternating cross-chain leadership serializes the natural faster branch and is not retained.

Restored the selected one-time post-factor high-priority schedule and capped the profiled sample-local solve kernel from its natural 120 registers/thread to 96, testing greater co-residency for the two grid64 solve fleets and wide updates. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 regressed from uncapped Trial4 1767.933 to 1872.220 us; aggregate measured 775.988 us. The cap's code-generation/spill cost outweighs any added overlap, so the natural register allocation remains selected.

Lowered the sample-local solve cap from 96 to 80 registers/thread, the first cap permitting three 256-thread CTAs by registers, while retaining the selected one-time post-factor DAG. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 recovered from cap96's 1872.220 to 1792.370 us but remained above uncapped Trial4's 1767.933; aggregate was outlier-inflated to 778.926 by untouched n256. Three-block residency does not repay the additional spill/code-generation cost.

Built a hybrid captured DAG: the first four 256-wide stages use Trial4's independent post-factor-staggered sample chains, then all side queues join the caller graph and the remaining twelve stages use grid2 factors, grid128 solves, and batch2 CuTe rank-k nodes through the same kernels' batched mode. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 measured 1785.312 us (1782.896 best), above full-split Trial4's 1767.933/1763.120; aggregate was broadly degraded to 784.846 across untouched cells. Rejoining after four stages does not recover the parent launch advantage enough to offset its lost overlap.

Moved the hybrid join from four to eight 256-wide stages, preserving independent overlap through the heavy first half and batching the trailing half. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 improved from split4 Trial14's 1785.312 to 1772.448 us (1768.976 best), but remained above full-split Trial4's 1767.933/1763.120; aggregate measured 774.467 us with slower untouched large cells. The cutoff trend favors retaining more independent stages.

Completed the 4/8/12/full split-stage bracket by joining after twelve 256-wide stages and batching only the final four stages. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 reached a branch target low of 1756.878 us (1754.176 best), improving split8's 1772.448 and full-split Trial4's 1767.933/1763.120 by 11.055/8.944 us. Aggregate was outlier-inflated to 784.965 by untouched n256/n512/n1024/n2048 cells. Late-stage batched launch efficiency now outweighs independent overlap only for the final quarter.

Refined the hybrid join to fourteen independent stages followed by two batched tail stages. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 reached a new branch target low of 1756.215 us (1752.096 best), edging split12 Trial16's 1756.878/1754.176 and improving full-split Trial4's 1767.933/1763.120. Aggregate reached 772.741 us despite a slower untouched n32768 cell. The gain is concentrated in batching the very small tail.

Moved the hybrid join to fifteen independent stages and only the final stage batched. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 regressed to 1784.342 us from split14 Trial17's 1756.215, while aggregate was outlier-inflated to 778.633 across untouched n256/n512/n2048/n4096 cells. Batching both final stages is required for the tail gain; batching only the factor-only final stage loses the stage14 interaction.

Completed the hybrid join bracket at thirteen independent stages followed by three batched tail stages. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 reached the branch target low of 1748.736 us (1743.872 best), improving cutoff12 Trial16 1756.878, cutoff14 Trial17 1756.215, and full-split Trial4 1767.933. Aggregate reached 772.009 us versus parent 768.640. The transition is bracketed on both sides and selects a three-stage batched tail.

Added a batch2/n4096-only CuTe rank-k operator whose persistent scheduler caps each one-matrix independent update to half the available clusters, allowing two sample updates and narrow work to coexist; the cutoff13 batched tail and every other dispatch retained the original full-grid operator. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 measured 1764.336 us versus full-grid cutoff13 Trial19's 1748.736; aggregate measured 772.727 us. Halving each wide grid extends its waves more than concurrent coexistence recovers, so full-grid independent updates remain selected.

Completed the independent CuTe persistent-grid sweep at three-quarter clusters, retaining the selected cutoff13 hybrid. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 measured 1759.048 us, between half-grid Trial20's 1764.336 and the original full-grid cutoff13 Trial19's 1748.736; aggregate was broadly degraded to 782.901 across untouched cells. Full persistent grids remain the measured winner.

Split the batch2/n4096 upper-triangle preparation into one 256-block copy kernel per sample on two equal-priority streams, joined before graph replay, while retaining Trial21's three-quarter independent rank-k grids and cutoff13 batched tail. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 benchmark cells passed. Batch2/n4096 regressed to 1788.798 us (1776.784 best) from Trial21's 1759.048 and the selected full-grid Trial19's 1748.736; aggregate measured 788.995 us and was additionally inflated by an untouched n256 timing outlier. Separate copy launches and event joins cost more than the original single batched 512-block copy.

Captured fresh-input upper preparation inside an input-identity-keyed batch2/n4096 graph, splitting each sample at the first 256 rows: two copy streams release their sample's narrow factor/solve chain after the prefix, while the first rank-k waits for that sample's remaining rows. Restored Trial19's selected full rank-k grids and cutoff13 tail. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 benchmark cells passed. Batch2/n4096 measured 1914.332 us with a 19.391 ms timing outlier, but its 1821.072 us best still trailed Trial19's 1743.872 best by 77.200 us; aggregate was 786.433 us. Four captured row-copy launches plus the extra stream/event DAG outweighed the intended copy/factor overlap.

Reduced captured preparation from four per-sample kernels to two batched row-range kernels on one copy stream: a 256-row prefix releases both narrow chains, and the suffix overlaps their first stage before gating rank-k. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 measured 1860.143 us with one 20.987 ms outlier across 200 runs; its 1760.752 us best improved Trial23 by 60.320 us but remained 16.880 us above selected Trial19's 1743.872 best. Aggregate was 782.904 us. Batched splitting recovers most four-launch overhead, leaving a narrow timing gap to the original copy-before-graph path.

Widened the batched captured-copy prefix from 256 to 512 rows per sample, trading some overlap for a fuller 64-CTA prefix wave before releasing the narrow chains. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 measured 1832.620 us with one 15.497 ms outlier; best improved slightly from Trial24's 1760.752 to 1758.720 us, still 14.848 us above selected Trial19's 1743.872. Aggregate was outlier-inflated to 793.034 us by the untouched n256 cell. A fuller prefix modestly reduces the captured split's best-case overhead.

Expanded the captured batched-copy prefix to 1024 rows per sample before releasing the narrow chains, leaving a 3072-row suffix to overlap. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 measured 1872.993 us with one 24.333 ms outlier; best improved from the 512-row Trial25's 1758.720 to 1757.136 us, still 13.264 us above selected Trial19's 1743.872. Aggregate was outlier-inflated to 795.238 us by untouched n256 timing. Successively larger prefixes reduce the split-copy penalty, showing that copy/narrow contention is outweighing overlap.

Expanded the captured batched-copy prefix to 2048 rows per sample, completing the coarse 256/512/1024/2048 release sweep. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 measured 1885.170 us with one 24.926 ms outlier; best regressed to 1764.816 us from the 1024-row Trial26's 1757.136, while aggregate was 786.266 us. The captured split is bracketed at 1024 rows, but even that best trails selected Trial19 by 13.264 us.

Eliminated the captured prefix copy: the first 256-row MathDx factor/solve stage now reads original accumulators directly from the input-specific graph pointer while writing its complete factored top panel, concurrent with one batched suffix copy for rows 256:4096; first rank-k joins both. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 measured 1847.587 us with one 23.058 ms outlier over 200 runs; best reached a new branch low of 1737.120 us, 6.752 us faster than selected Trial19's 1743.872 best, and the outlier-excluded mean is about 1741.0 us. Aggregate was outlier-inflated to 782.127 us. Direct-input initialization removes the prefix delay and exposes useful copy/narrow overlap.

Removed batch2/n4096 preparation entirely. The input-keyed graph's first 256-row MathDx stage reads its initial diagonal/panel accumulators directly from fresh input, and a distinct CuTe rank-k uses the original trailing matrix as C while writing updated D into output; subsequent stages remain in-place. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 measured 1758.575 us with one 12.081 ms outlier over 200 runs; best reached 1700.896 us, improving Trial28's 1737.120 and selected Trial19's 1743.872 by 36.224/42.976 us, with an outlier-excluded mean about 1706.7 us. Aggregate measured 776.871 us. Direct source/destination rank-k removes the profiled 31.9 us preparation and its dependency.

Re-tested simultaneous sample-chain release after removing input preparation, deleting the one-factor stagger event so both direct-input narrow chains start at graph entry. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 measured 1767.902 us with one 12.337 ms outlier; best regressed to 1711.104 us from staggered Trial29's 1700.896, and the outlier-excluded mean is about 1714.8 us versus Trial29's ~1706.7. Aggregate was 780.909 us. The roughly 20-us first-factor stagger remains beneficial even after preparation is eliminated.

Completed the direct-input initial-stagger bracket by releasing sample1 after sample0's first factor plus first 64-CTA solve instead of immediately after the factor. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 measured 2060.019 us with one 64.589 ms outlier; best regressed to 1734.608 us versus factor-only stagger Trial29's 1700.896 and equal-start Trial30's 1711.104. Aggregate was 789.861 us. The factor-only release remains the measured scheduler point.

Joined only the first direct-input update: after the factor-only stagger, both sample stage-0 narrow panels rendezvous for one batch2 separate-C/D CuTe rank-k, then the remaining twelve independent stages and three batched tail stages retain Trial29's topology. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 measured 1857.222 us with one 23.854 ms outlier; best regressed to 1741.808 us from independent Trial29's 1700.896. Aggregate was 785.282 us. Preserving the first update's per-sample independence is worth substantially more than eliminating one rank-k launch.

Profile-guided Trial33 restored Trial29's independent first updates and capped only its distinct source-C/D rank-k at 60 clusters, exactly dividing 120 triangular work tiles into two per active cluster instead of a 74+46 partial wave. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed, but batch2/n4096 best regressed to 1727.392 us from Trial29's 1700.896; mean 1846.193 included one 24.441 ms outlier and aggregate was 797.963 us. Profile-guided source-only 128x128 one-CTA rank-k reduced the intended tile/shared footprint while leaving all later updates unchanged. The wrapped local build passed because CuTe compilation is GPU-conditional, but wrapped Modal validation failed at import before test0: SM100's selected 2:1 MMA atom rejected cluster shape (1,1) as not divisible. No validation or benchmark metric was produced; no additional hosted profile was launched.

Fixed Trial34's compile-invalid one-CTA form with a legal 128x128 per-CTA, 2x2 cluster source-only rank-k, preserving each 256x256 triangular macrotile while distributing its shared staging across four CTAs. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 measured 1873.923 us with one 22.182 ms outlier; best regressed to 1765.392 us from profiled Trial29's 1700.896, and aggregate measured 782.903 us. Four-CTA cooperation costs far more than the profiled shared footprint/conflicts; the original 256x256 2x1 operator remains selected. No additional hosted request was launched.

Restored profiled Trial29's original 256x256 two-CTA source rank-k and changed only its two narrow queues from high to default priority, letting the profiled 70% no-eligible MathDx work and 81.5% no-eligible CuTe work share equal scheduling priority. Slice build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 measured 1759.333 us with one 12.419 ms outlier; best 1702.384 us was 1.488 us above high-priority Trial29's 1700.896 and within target noise, while the outlier-excluded mean was about 1705.8 us versus Trial29's about 1706.7. Aggregate reached 773.423 us. Queue priority is noise-flat after preparation removal, with the exact profiled high-priority commit retained as the conservative target floor. No additional hosted request was launched.

Its input-identity-keyed graph removes the 31.9-us preparation entirely: first-stage MathDx reads stable fresh input, first one-matrix CuTe updates use distinct source C/output D, two chains retain the factor-only stagger through 13 independent stages, and three tail stages batch. All build/17 tests/fresh-input guard/15 cells passed. Batch2/n4096 reached 1700.896 us best and about 1706.7 us excluding one 12.081-ms outlier, versus prior selected Trial19 1743.872 best/1748.736 mean and parent aggregate 768.640; noisy all-cell aggregate was 776.871. Measured alternatives: split-copy bests 1760.752/1758.720/1757.136/1764.816, direct-input suffix-copy 1737.120, simultaneous/factor-plus-solve stagger 1711.104/1734.608, batched first source update 1741.808, source cap60 1727.392, legal 128x128 2x2 source cluster 1765.392, and equal-priority source 1702.384; 128x128 1x1 was compile-invalid.
